summary_paragraph: Mr. Johnson, a patient with hepatocellular carcinoma in the setting of hepatitis C and alcoholic cirrhosis, was admitted for his second transarterial chemoembolization (TACE) of a recurrent liver tumor. The procedure was performed successfully, after which he developed expected post-embolization symptoms including mild abdominal pain and nausea. On the second hospital day, he experienced rigors and was found to have a new left lower lobe pneumonia on chest X-ray, for which he was started on oral levofloxacin. His liver enzymes rose as expected, and his platelet count remained low but stable. He improved clinically, with resolution of chills and nausea, and was discharged home on day four. He was sent home with a five-day course of antibiotics, continued vancomycin and Florastor for C. difficile prevention, and pain and nausea medications as needed. Follow-up was arranged with his hepatology and transplant teams.
problems: Intestinal infection due to Clostridium difficile
